stories.headline: Anthropic IPO: pricing set for Nov 18 at up to $1.4tn, with investor and rival scrutiny
stories.claim: Anthropic has filed to offer 825 million shares at $70-$78 each, with pricing set for 18 November and trading to start the next day.
stories.summary: Anthropic is preparing a Nasdaq listing that could value the AI company at up to about $1.4 trillion, one of the largest IPOs ever. Its updated filing offers 825 million shares priced between $70 and $78 each, and at the top of the range the sale would raise $64.35 billion. Pricing is planned for 18 November, with trading under the ticker ANT starting the following day. Earlier filings showed the seven founders, led by CEO Dario Amodei, planning to sell about $250 million each, and reports say the founders hold about 50.1% of most votes despite owning roughly 22% of shares. A separate $26 billion private placement involving Nvidia and Alphabet sits outside the public offering and could push total capital raised above SpaceX's June IPO. Reports that several banks have turned away buy orders from mainland Chinese and Hong Kong investors, citing ITAR export rules, could narrow the investor base. Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up 1,206% year on year, and reports suggest the offering is heavily oversubscribed and underwriters may price above the range.

stories.headline: Google turned to AMD Epyc, not its own Axion chips, to secure its first confidential TPU
stories.claim: Google's eighth-generation TPU 8tx for confidential AI uses AMD Epyc CPUs rather than its own Axion chips.
stories.summary: Google has added the TPU 8tx to its eighth-generation TPU family, a system for confidential AI that pairs its accelerator with AMD's 5th Gen Epyc CPUs rather than its own Axion chips. Google says the 8tx offers up to 2x lower latency than the TPU 8t, and is aimed at regulated enterprises and governments that want to train models on private data. AMD says its Secure Encrypted Virtualization extends protection to the accelerators, a first for cloud TPUs. The 8tx reuses existing chips rather than new designs, and Google reportedly chose Turin to match PCIe Gen5 interfaces. AMD shares closed up 13.26% at $508.58 on 9 November, though the move also reflected other factors. Analysts see the deal as a sign of closer ties, but not a confirmed accelerator partnership.

Google has not explained why it did not use its own Axion chips; a previous unconfirmed report suggested AMD may collaborate on a future TPU.

stories.headline: Tanker strikes docked American Heritage cruise ship in New Orleans; port sues owners
stories.claim: A loaded tanker struck the docked American Heritage cruise ship in New Orleans; the Port of New Orleans has sued the tanker's owners.
stories.summary: The Port of New Orleans sued the owners and managers of the tanker Atlantic Asphalt on Saturday, seeking more than $1m and asking that the vessel be seized and sold. The suit names Nave Shipping SA, a subsidiary of China State Shipbuilding Corporation, and manager Thome Ship Management, and was filed in federal court in the Eastern District of Louisiana. The loaded tanker struck the docked American Heritage, a American Cruise Lines paddlewheel river ship, on the Mississippi at about 12:30pm on Friday, causing it to tilt and partly take on water. The ship had 197 passengers aboard, and 32 people were taken to hospital, mostly with bumps and bruises, including two harbour police officers. New Orleans' mayor called it a 'miracle on the Mississippi' because no one was killed or critically hurt. The Coast Guard said the tanker apparently lost steering, though the cause is under investigation. Many passengers lost IDs, phones and belongings, and the city is providing food, hotels and transport.

stories.headline: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop caused by copper-to-fibre upgrade failure
stories.claim: The FAA lifted a rare nationwide ground stop on Friday evening after nearly five hours, blamed on a telecom failure during copper-to-fibre work; recovery is expected before Thanksgiving.
stories.summary: The FAA lifted a rare nationwide ground stop at about 8.15pm Eastern on Friday, ending nearly five hours of disruption that halted US departures. Officials blamed a telecommunications failure during routine work replacing old copper lines with fibre at a remote FAA facility, and said there was no sign of a cyberattack. Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said a newly installed router flooded other air traffic control routers with more than 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds, disrupting radar feeds and communications with aircraft, while the root cause, possibly faulty hardware, a misconfigured router or contractor error by L3Harris, remains under investigation. More than 6,700 flights were cancelled on Friday and over 25,000 delayed, according to FlightAware, and JetBlue cancelled all domestic flights. Cancellations continued into the weekend, with more than 6,000 on Saturday, and about 4,000 aircraft that were airborne all landed safely. About 1.5 million travellers were affected, according to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Duffy has pressed Congress for $30 billion, later saying up to $50 billion, to modernise the air traffic control system, and normal operations are expected before Thanksgiving on 26 November.
key_points: The FAA lifted the first nationwide ground stop since January 2023 at about 8.15pm Eastern on Friday, after nearly five hours.
Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said a newly installed router flooded other air traffic control routers with over 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds.
More than 6,700 flights were cancelled on Friday and over 25,000 delayed, with JetBlue cancelling all domestic flights.
Cancellations continued with more than 6,000 on Saturday, and normal schedules are not expected until late Sunday.
About 1.5 million travellers were affected, according to House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries.
Duffy has asked Congress for $30 billion, later saying up to $50 billion, to modernise air traffic control; L3Harris has completed more than 70% of the planned conversion.
stories.market_take: Airlines could see short-term disruption costs, though the impact appears limited now the stop has been lifted.

stories.headline: Researchers say Chinese AI models were trained on banned Nvidia Blackwell GPUs
stories.claim: Independent researchers claim Chinese open-weight AI models show fingerprints of training on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs banned for China; the claim is unreviewed.
stories.summary: Independent researchers, including former OpenAI engineer Will DePue through his consultancy Unemployment Labs, claim several Chinese AI models were trained on Nvidia's Blackwell GPUs, which US export controls restrict for China. The team says it matched weight-initialisation patterns of open-weight models against more than six trillion chip and seed combinations, finding conclusive evidence for six models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3.1 and MiniMax-M3, with Ling-3.1-Flash also named. The team says AMD cards did not match the weight pattern for DeepSeek V4. The analysis has not been peer reviewed, and the researchers stress that it identifies the chip type only, not where the chips were physically located, how they were accessed, or whether any export rule was broken. Renting Blackwell hardware abroad, including from US cloud providers, is not clearly illegal, and the method works only on open-weight models. The claims arrive as several bills pending in Congress seek to tighten chip export rules, and they bear on Nvidia's China exposure and on enforcement of export controls.
key_points: Former OpenAI engineer Will DePue and the group Unemployment Labs claim several Chinese AI models were trained on Nvidia Blackwell GPUs, which US export controls restrict for China.
The team says six models, including DeepSeek-V4-Pro, Kimi K3.1 and MiniMax-M3, show conclusive Blackwell fingerprints, with Ling-3.1-Flash also named.
The method compares weight-initialisation patterns against more than six trillion chip and seed combinations, and AMD cards did not match the DeepSeek V4 pattern.
The analysis has not been peer reviewed and cannot show where the chips were located or how they were accessed, so US cloud providers could be involved.
The researchers say no export rule has been shown to be broken, and renting Blackwell hardware abroad is not clearly illegal.
The claims come as several bills in Congress seek to tighten chip export controls, bearing on Nvidia's China exposure.
stories.likelihood_reason: The method is clever and was tested against alternatives, but it is a single independent research group's inference and has not been independently replicated or confirmed by the companies or US officials.
signals: Companies not reported to have responded
stories.market_take: If confirmed, it would reinforce the value of Nvidia's China market and could prompt tighter export enforcement that affects Nvidia and cloud rental providers.

stocks.reason: Its chips were tested as an alternative and ruled out, but tighter controls could affect its China sales too.

stories.headline: Lilly says its obesity drugs helped patients lose weight in clinical trials
stories.claim: Eli Lilly released new trial data for its obesity drugs, showing large weight loss in adults and adolescents.
stories.summary: Eli Lilly has released fresh data from several obesity trials ahead of the ObesityWeek 2026 medical conference, showing sharp weight loss. In a Phase 2 trial, its experimental combination of eloralintide and tirzepatide, called EloraTZP, cut weight by up to an average of 23.3% at 48 weeks in adults with type 2 diabetes. Up to 60% of those participants no longer met the obesity BMI threshold. In Phase 3 SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS trials, Zepbound reduced BMI by an average of 21.4% at 72 weeks in teenagers with obesity. The full results have not yet been published, so the figures are preliminary company data.

EloraTZP also lowered A1C by up to 2.9%, with up to 77% reaching normal blood sugar.
Zepbound cut BMI by an average of 21.4% at 72 weeks in adolescents aged 12 to 18.
Full results have not yet been released, so the data remain preliminary.
stories.market_take: Positive trial data supports Lilly's obesity franchise, though full results will matter more for investors.

stories.headline: Francophone Summit Opens With DR Congo, Rwandan Clash
stories.claim: A French-speaking nations summit opened in Phnom Penh amid a row over DR Congo's threat to quit if Rwanda's candidate wins.
stories.summary: A summit of French-speaking nations opened in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, with Emmanuel Macron attending, but the talks are dominated by a dispute between DR Congo and Rwanda. Rwanda's Louise Mushikiwabo, who has led the Organisation Internationale de la Francophonie for eight years, is seeking a third term, and Kinshasa has threatened to quit if she is re-elected on Monday. DR Congo accuses Rwanda of backing the M23 rebels, which Kigali denies, and it has put forward Juliana Lumumba as its candidate. Macron has urged unity, and Rwanda says he asked Kagame to withdraw its candidate, a request it rejected. The organisation has 53 full members, and Canada is its second-largest donor.

stories.headline: Floods Force Gaza to Choose Between Clean Water and Pumping Out Sewage
stories.claim: Flooding in Gaza's displacement camps, worsened by damaged sewers and fuel shortages, is forcing a trade-off between pumping water out and drinking water.
stories.summary: Storms over 7 and 8 November flooded tents across Gaza, with the Government Media Office saying at least 70,000 tents were affected within 12 hours. In Al Maghazi camp, municipal engineer Imad Abdel Jawad says pumps run on diesel meant for the wells that supply drinking water, so pumping out floodwater takes away fuel needed for clean water. Damaged and stolen sewer manhole covers let rainwater overwhelm sewage networks, and replacement parts are scarce under Israeli restrictions, according to the UN humanitarian office OCHA. OCHA estimates 1.4 million people, 65 per cent of Gaza's population, live in tents or shelters. Clinics report rising cases of respiratory and stomach illnesses in children as the rainy season begins.
key_points: Rainstorms on 7 and 8 November flooded shelters across Gaza, with at least 70,000 tents affected within 12 hours, according to Gaza's Government Media Office.

stories.headline: Muslim Association of Britain designated terror group by Egypt
stories.claim: Egypt has added the Muslim Association of Britain to its terrorism list, alongside 34 other organisations and 36 individuals.
stories.summary: Egypt has designated the Muslim Association of Britain (MAB) as a terrorist group, placing it on a terrorism list with 35 organisations and 36 individuals, ordered by a Cairo Criminal Court last week for five years. The MAB, a partner of the Stop the War Coalition, has organised pro-Palestine marches in the UK, and was earlier designated by the United Arab Emirates. The group has been linked by some to a former Hamas chief, Muhammad Kathem Sawalha, a claim the MAB denies. It rejects the accusations, calls the Egyptian move political, and says the British citizens Alaa Abd el-Fattah and Eman el-Shazly were treated unfairly by Egyptian courts. Security commentators say UK agencies may now look more closely at the group, though there is no UK government action reported.

stories.headline: Weeks after shipment was swiped by China, Pentagon ‘struggles to account for’ $31 billion in missing F-35 aircraft parts
stories.claim: A GAO report says the Pentagon cannot accurately track about 26 million F-35 spare parts worth an estimated $31 billion.
stories.summary: A Government Accountability Office report published this week says the Pentagon struggles to track around 26 million F-35 spare parts, estimated to be worth $31 billion. The watchdog described the inventory system as outdated, inaccurate and incomplete, and said the Department of Defense has made minimal progress on earlier recommendations. The findings come weeks after classified F-35 parts were reportedly diverted through Hong Kong by a UPS worker and allegedly taken by China in September. The programme is estimated to cost $1.9 trillion over its lifetime. The Pentagon says a live data link with prime contractors is being built to close the gaps, but the report raises doubts about the readiness and reliability of the fleet.

stories.headline: These ‘Ghostly’ Galaxies Have Lost Their Dark Matter
stories.claim: Three dark-matter-deficient galaxies may have formed from a head-on collision, which also supports dark matter being a physical substance.
stories.summary: Three faint galaxies about 65 million light-years away, DF2, DF4 and DF9, appear to contain little or no dark matter, which astronomers had thought almost impossible. A June 2026 paper in The Astrophysical Journal proposes that two ordinary galaxies collided, leaving the gas and dust clumped while the dark matter passed straight through, creating three dark-matter-free galaxies. Researchers say this undermines modified-gravity alternatives, since the galaxies' formation fits the idea that dark matter is a real physical substance. Dark matter makes up about 27% of the universe and remains undetected directly, with candidates including neutrinos, WIMPs and primordial black holes. The findings are a scientific advance rather than a direct detection.
key_points: DF2, DF4 and DF9 are faint galaxies that seem to contain little or no dark matter.
DF2 was found in 2018, DF4 in 2019 and DF9 was added in 2026.

Dark matter has still not been detected directly, and its exact nature is unknown.

It is an art and design work rather than a business story, but it adds to a growing run of speculative design that uses dystopian imagery to make climate concerns tangible.

stories.headline: Jaime Hayon's sculptural football table rules the roost
stories.claim: Jaime Hayon has designed the RS Capsule, a sculptural football table made by Barcelona firm RS Barcelona.
stories.summary: Spanish designer Jaime Hayon has turned the humble football table into a sculptural object with the RS Capsule, made by RS Barcelona, a family-run metalworking firm founded in 1975 on the outskirts of Barcelona. The table features a curvaceous aluminium form, cast aluminium players shaped like Hayon's signature 'Chicken' figure, and a warm, woody beige powder-coated finish. The collaboration began in 2022 and took shape after Rafael Rodríguez visited Hayon's Valencia studio in 2024. A glossy anodised version is in development. The piece is a design launch aimed at a premium market rather than a mass-market product.
key_points: RS Barcelona, founded in 1975 and run by brothers Rafael and Sergio Rodríguez, has produced the RS Capsule with Jaime Hayon.
The table has curved aluminium legs and internal mechanisms, with players in the form of Hayon's 13.5cm cast aluminium 'Chicken'.
The collaboration began in 2022, and the design was developed in the factory after a 2024 studio visit in Valencia.
A glossy all-over anodised aluminium version is currently under development.

stories.headline: Take an early look as Wim Wenders sets his sights on Swiss architect Peter Zumthor in a new 3D film
stories.claim: Wim Wenders' 3D documentary on architect Peter Zumthor, From Inside Out, will be released across Europe from 26 November 2026.
stories.summary: Wim Wenders' new 3D documentary, From Inside Out: The Architecture of Peter Zumthor, takes 14 years to make and follows the Swiss architect's buildings as living places shaped by light and the people who use them. The film visits sites including a retreat in Devon, the $724m Los Angeles County Museum of Art (LACMA), the Steilneset memorial in Norway and the newly opened Beyeler Foundation extension in Basel. Wenders presented it at the Venice Film Festival, and it will be released across Europe from 26 November 2026. Zumthor's wife Annalisa, who died before release, also appears. The film is a cultural and architectural release rather than a market story.
key_points: From Inside Out is Wenders' tenth 3D film and took 14 years to make.
It covers Zumthor's buildings, including LACMA in Los Angeles (a $724m project), a Devon retreat and the Beyeler Foundation extension in Basel.
Wenders praises Zumthor's perfectionism and his limited output of around 20 buildings.
The film will be released across Europe from 26 November 2026, with further details to follow.

stories.headline: Sona Listening Practices / Épico Studio
stories.claim: Épico Estudio and Panorama have designed Sona, a device-free listening space in Mexico City's Condesa district.
stories.summary: A 245 square metre listening venue called Sona has opened in the Condesa neighbourhood of Mexico City, designed by Épico Estudio with Panorama. Founded by a group of friends led by Luis López, known as Lulo, the space is built around sonic immersion and is device-free, alcohol-free and free of distractions. The architects present listening as a deliberate, shared and deeply sensory act. The project is a niche cultural interior rather than a major building, but it shows how design can shape social habits around sound.

stories.headline: Plissè Block Is A Pleated Glass Sofa That Refuses to Blend In
stories.claim: Luca Ricci designed Plissè Block, a pleated glass sofa with red velvet cushions, as a custom piece for Fivefourfive's Milan store.
stories.summary: A sofa made of fluted glass and red velvet has been created as a custom piece for the Milan store of fashion label Fivefourfive. Designed by Luca Ricci, the Plissè Block is built from three modules, with two side blocks flanking a central section, and its outer fluted glass layer wraps a smooth inner support layer. Its pleated surface echoes folded fabric, while three cylindrical backrests and three rectangular seat cushions in red velvet add colour and softer forms. The reviewer praises how the piece gives a heavy furniture shape a lighter, more expressive presence in a retail setting. The article also notes open questions about comfort and durability, since no glass specifications or load testing were reported.
key_points: Designer Luca Ricci created Plissè Block as a custom piece for fashion label Fivefourfive's Milan store.
The sofa has three modules, with a smooth inner glass layer and a fluted outer glass layer.
Red velvet seat cushions and cylindrical backrests give the transparent frame colour and contrast.
The pleated surface references fabric pleating, and small metal fittings add visible construction detail.
The article says the images do not show comfort or durability, and no load testing was reported.

stories.headline: Mexico's Parque del Jaguar protects jaguars with 18-kilometre limestone wall
stories.claim: Colectivo C733 has completed an 18-km dry-stacked limestone wall and visitor buildings at Parque del Jaguar in Tulum, Mexico.
stories.summary: Mexican studio Colectivo C733 has built an 18-kilometre dry-stacked limestone wall that protects more than 1,000 hectares of forest at Parque del Jaguar in Tulum. The wall is built without mortar, so jaguars and other wildlife can pass through gaps between the stones while the perimeter still marks the protected area. The park combines public buildings, viewing towers and a suspended canopy walkway with low-impact transport, while new construction is concentrated in areas already altered. The project also includes soil remediation, reforestation, asphalt removal and the recovery of water systems. It responds to habitat disruption from roads, development and tourism around the ancient Mayan site of Tulum.
key_points: An 18-kilometre dry-stacked limestone wall, based on traditional Mayan stone boundaries, encloses more than 1,000 hectares of forest.
The wall has gaps that let wildlife move through, which helps jaguar habitat connectivity.
The central entrance complex includes a museum, cafe, shop, multipurpose room and open-air forum.
Visitor routes use pedestrian, cycling and electric transport, and new buildings sit in previously altered areas.
The project includes soil remediation, reforestation and removal of asphalt from previously developed land.

stories.headline: This beachside office in Thailand, made of reclaimed elements, is our new favourite workspace
stories.claim: Bangkok Design Studio's Boonserm Premthada has built Traces By The Sea, a reclaimed-timber office in Khao Lak, Thailand.
stories.summary: A beachside office in Khao Lak, Thailand, is built largely from reclaimed timber salvaged from an old rice cooperative building in Phatthalung and a wooden school in Phang Nga. Designed by Boonserm Premthada of Bangkok Design Studio, the project spans four timber volumes linked by decks and walkways. Large woven bamboo trays from northeastern Thailand, traditionally used in silkworm rearing, serve as exterior sun shades. The design keeps the reclaimed pieces' original paint, joints and surfaces, and relies on natural ventilation and shade rather than mechanical cooling. Premthada says the scheme reflects Thai domestic traditions of living with the climate.
key_points: The office, called Traces By The Sea, is in Khao Lak on Thailand's west coast.
Its timber comes from an old rice cooperative building in Phatthalung and a wooden school in Phang Nga.
Four separate volumes are connected by decks and walkways.
Woven bamboo trays act as sun shades, while openings provide ventilation and daylight.
The architect is known for earlier projects, including a tower of elephant dung bricks and his own house.

stories.headline: Andy Burnham vows to reopen Brexit debate as he paves way for UK-EU ‘reset’ deal
stories.claim: Andy Burnham, now PM, plans to reopen the Brexit debate and sign a UK-EU reset deal in Brussels on Friday.
stories.summary: Andy Burnham, who has succeeded Keir Starmer as prime minister, used a speech at the Lord Mayor's Banquet to argue that Brexit has diminished Britain and that the debate should be reopened. Ahead of a UK-EU summit in Brussels on Friday, he is expected to sign a reset deal including a food and drink agreement under which Britain would adopt EU plant and animal standards, a youth mobility scheme allowing EU nationals under 30 to live and work in Britain (about 80,000 people for three years), and an energy deal. He has said the deal is only a beginning, and a longer-term options paper on the relationship is to inform decisions in the next parliament, with rejoining the single market or customs union among the options. Supporters of Brexit, including Nigel Farage, are expected to protest. Markets may watch sterling and UK-facing stocks for signs of closer alignment.
key_points: Burnham is expected to sign a UK-EU reset deal in Brussels on Friday, including food and drink alignment with EU standards.
The deal would include a youth mobility scheme allowing about 80,000 people under 30 to live and work across the UK and EU for three years.
Burnham said the deal is a starting point and options on the long-term relationship will be presented to inform the next parliament.
Options reportedly include rejoining the EU, the single market or the customs union, with the public having the final say.
Critics such as Nigel Farage are expected to challenge the move in Brussels.
stories.market_take: Closer UK-EU ties could support sterling and UK-exposed sectors, though details are not yet set out.
